holes_found.description: OBS-D-01 duration-prong evidence independence is overstated. The frozen OBS-D-01 conjunction requires the MAX totality duration to match 138.2 s within +/-10 s (i.e. observed max in [128.2,148.2] s). The verdict evidence_duration string reads “~138 s max central-line reported; matches NASA 138.2 s within +/-10 s.” But the greatest-eclipse maximum occurs off Iceland’s west coast over open ocean (NASA/national sources + web confirmation: ‘reaching its maximum duration off Iceland’s west coast’), where there was no ground observer; the cleanest INDEPENDENT post-event ground durations are ~88-110 s (Iberian mainland) and ~59-90 s (Iceland). The single source cited at ~138 s (ScienceDaily/Space.com aggregate) is dated in part 2026-08-10 — PRE-event — i.e. it is NASA’s precomputed catalog value restated, not an independent post-event measurement. Using bucket_1’s own predicted value to confirm bucket_1’s duration prong is mildly circular and hands a dome defender the exact ‘you cited a pre-event number as post-event confirmation’ gotcha we criticize the dome for.
holes_found.recommendation: Reword evidence_duration in the EXP commission file / any surfaced prose to separate (i) NASA-computed central-line max 138.2 s at the greatest-eclipse point off Iceland’s W coast (no ground observer; corroborated as a prediction, not an independent post-event datum) from (ii) independently observed ground durations of ~59-110 s. Crucially, add the one sentence that makes the dome-falsification robust to this: EVERY observed single-station duration (59-110 s) already exceeds the dome-forced <=7 s bound by 8-16x, so OBS-D-01’s dome-falsification conclusion does not depend on whether the 138 s max was directly observed. This strengthens the verdict and removes the attack surface; no verdict change.
